newsitem.title: GERMANY: Christmas opening hours muddle hits German shops.
newsitem.headline: Christmas opening hours muddle hits German shops.

text.p: German shopowners found stores emptying early on the second Saturday of the all-important Christmas season, as consumer confusion over new shop hours knocked 10 percent off turnover.

Germany's HDE retailers association, in a lightning survey of 60 big stores, said that the weather -- which was crisp and clear -- was not to blame. Plenty of people went to the shops, but few opened their wallets.
"For many people stores seem to be a sort of walk-in shop window," the HDE's Thomas Werz said on Saturday evening.

German retailers, hit by four years of stagnating business, had been hoping the scrapping of old rules limiting store opening hours would spur new business -- especially in the runup to Christmas, when they make a third of annual turnover.
Shops can stay open until 6 p.m. in the four Saturdays of Advent -- even later than the new closing time of 4 p.m.
But department stores contacted around the country by Reuters said there was still confusion among consumers over when the shopping stops on Saturdays.
"The reality didn't live up to our expectations," said a spokesman for department store Karstadt in Munich.
The spokesman lamented that his store had emptied at mid-afternoon, despite a publicity drive to tell shoppers that they could stay late.
"Business was around the same as last year -- but we live from growth," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
Under the new shop hours, introduced at the start of November, consumers can also shop late until 8 p.m. on weekdays and some traditional Saturday business has shifted there.
"We have had a very good week, with pluses from Monday through to Friday, so the weaker Saturday can be seen in context," the Karstadt spokesman said.
The HDE's Werz confirmed the trend, saying late weekday shopping was catching on after a slow start in November.

The picture was similar elsewhere in Germany, with the recently reopened KaDeWe in Berlin -- the country's largest department store -- reporting an improvement this Saturday after a disappointing start a week earlier.

Store owners are pinning their hopes this year on a busy final week before Christmas. The final shopping Saturday falls favourably on December 21 and many people will be off work and ready to buy last-minute presents on the 23rd, a Monday.
"We expect really good business in the last week before Christmas," a spokeswoman at the Hertie chain in Dresden said.
